name: Epilogue
tagline: Day 30. The hearing. The house. What it's for.
notes: Plays after Lukey's arc is finished (and podcast ep4). Shows the Day 30 hearing, then the final house choice (sets flag.house_choice: 1 = sell, 2 = stay, 3 = demolish), then the matching epilogue for Lukey's ending.

lines: *The house isn't finished yet. Something under the kitchen sink is still dripping.*
*Day 30. City Hall. The condemnation hearing takes four minutes.*
*Inspector Dan stands up, clears his throat and tells the council that 12 Heartbreak Lane is the safest it has been since 1926.*
*The order is lifted. Somebody in the back row honks a clown horn. It's Mr. Giggles. Nobody knows why he's there.*
*That night, you stand alone in the kitchen. It's quiet. It's dry. It's fixed. For real.*
*Day 30. City Hall. The condemnation hearing takes four minutes.*
*Inspector Dan stands up, clears his throat and tells the council that 12 Heartbreak Lane is the safest it has been since 1926.*
*The order is lifted. Somebody in the back row honks a clown horn. It's Mr. Giggles. Nobody knows why he's there.*
*That night, you stand in the kitchen. It's quiet. It's dry. And you're not alone: Lukey is sitting on the counter, swinging his legs.*
Lukey: So, boss. What are we doing with it?
*The house is fixed. Now you have to decide what it's for.*

choices.text: Sell it. And take Lukey with you.
Fix it for real, and sell it to someone who'll love it.
Fix it for real, and sell it to someone who'll love it.
Fix it for real, and sell it to someone who'll love it.
Let it go. Too much happened here.
Let it go. Too much happened here.
Let it go. Too much happened here.
Let it go. Too much happened here.

lines: *You sell 12 Heartbreak Lane to a young couple with a baby on the way. Dan signs off on it with a pun nobody gets but you.*
*Lukey cries the whole drive to your new place. Not sad crying. Just a LOT of water. You have to run the wipers on the inside of the car.*
*Three days after you move in, the kitchen faucet in your new apartment starts to drip.*
You: Lukey.
Lukey: What? New house. A guy's gotta make an entrance.
*He's already glaring at your new dishwasher.*
*You stay. Obviously you stay.*
*The flipper finally has a house she isn't going to flip. It has a pink rug, a forgiven dishwasher and a ghost who cooks pasta by yelling at you.*
*Dan comes to Sunday dinner every week. He tells the same jokes his dad does. Lukey mouths along to every single one.*
Lukey: He gets the timing from me.
You: He gets the timing from his mom.
Lukey: ...Yeah, okay. He gets the timing from his mom.
*You let the city have the house. It held too much. Lukey agrees, on one condition: you take the sink.*
*You take the sink.*
*It sits in the kitchen of your new place, connected to nothing, perfectly dry. Lukey naps in it like a cat.*
*The old lot becomes a little park with a drinking fountain that never stops dripping.*
Lukey: That's not me.
*It's definitely him.*
*You still keep his old swim whistle on your keyring. It's never once made a sound, but you'd swear it's warm.*
*Every time a faucet drips anywhere, you give it a little two-finger salute. People have started to notice.*
*You keep his sticky note. 'FIXED IT MYSELF. MOSTLY.' It's framed now. It's earned it.*
*You sell 12 Heartbreak Lane to a young couple with a baby on the way.*
*At the closing, Dan shakes their hands and tells them the kitchen's got a real 'drip personality.' They don't get it. You do.*
*A year later they send you a photo: the baby in the kitchen, wearing a pair of tiny swim goggles. Dan's idea.*
*The next week, you buy another broken house. You fix that one for real, too.*
*Some nights, when the house is very quiet, the kitchen faucet hums a little Bon Jovi. Just a few bars. Just for you.*
*You finally make peace with the dishwasher. It's what he would have wanted. Eventually.*
*The flashlight he was so rude about lives in the drawer by the sink. You never quite manage to throw it out.*
*You don't sell. You can't. You fixed it too well to give it away.*
*Dan comes to Sunday dinner. He brings the goggles and sets them on the windowsill over the sink, where they belong.*
*The flipper has a home. It's quiet here now. A good quiet. The kind a house gets when everyone in it is finally home, or finally free.*
*You love him enough to let the place he died go, too.*
*You think Coach would get it. Some pools you just drain and start over.*
*Somewhere, someone is muttering that THEY would have done the demo better. You hold the flashlight anyway.*
*You let the city have it. Some places hold too much.*
*The lot becomes a little park. Dan cuts the ribbon. There's a drinking fountain by the gate.*
*It never stops dripping. Nobody can fix it. Nobody tries very hard.*
